summary: I wrote plan.md but haven't built or rendered anything, and I haven't dry-run the roof. The street is on the south side, not the north as asked, because the fixed sockets face south. The row is red brick with pale stone trim: two green-fascia shopfronts that open straight onto the counters, two stone oriel bays rising through the flats, a dark slate mansard, and a side stair bay holding the flats' own front door.
concept_subject: A Victorian high-street shop row in warm red brick with pale Bath-stone dressings. The street runs along the front, with a smooth stone pavement and a grey andesite kerb. Two shops on the ground floor have counters that open straight onto the pavement under one long horizontal opening. Each shop has a deep green fascia board with its name in white banner letters. Stone consoles separate the two fascias, and stone pilasters frame the ends. A dark-oak bracket at each end of the shopfront carries a hanging sign. A projecting stone cornice runs across the whole row above the shops. It carries two stone-framed oriel bay windows, one centred over each shop, which rise through both flat storeys with three-pane glazing on each floor. Tall narrow sash windows flank each oriel. A stone string course and stone sills and lintels give the brick its rhythm, with paired cut-stone quoins at the corners. On the right sits a narrower stair bay with a double dark-oak front door, a fanlight, a stone surround and a slab hood, plus a small FLATS sign. Above it all is a dark-slate mansard roof with a dentilled stone eaves cornice, an iron-bar crest and dormers lined up over the oriels. Three brick chimney stacks with stone bands and caps stand on the end walls and at the back, two of them trailing smoke. Behind the row is a cobbled yard with brick walls, gates and keeper doors.
concept_size: 24 wide (plus chimney breasts), 18 deep, 3 storeys plus mansard
